units.text: Shelfwise is the service that keeps track of how much stock each warehouse holds and reserves stock for incoming orders.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview

units.text: It is one deployable TypeScript service with a small admin front end.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview

units.text: At peak it handles about 3,000 reservations per hour.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview

units.text: This tour walks through the code by responsibility: what each group of modules owns, which files to open first, and how the groups depend on each other.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview

units.text: The groups are presentation, API and orchestration, domain services, supplier integration, persistence and external systems, and observability and error handling.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview

units.text: The admin web UI lives in `web/admin/`.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation

units.text: Warehouse staff use it to look up stock levels, place manual holds and review failed supplier imports.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation

units.text: It holds no stock logic of its own: every screen calls the service's REST API, and the UI never talks to the database directly.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Client and presentation

units.text: The HTTP handlers in `src/api/routes.ts` are the only entry point for requests.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: They validate the request body, attach a correlation ID and pass the work on; they contain no business rules.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: A `POST /reservations` request goes to the reservation orchestrator in `src/orders/reserve.ts`.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: The reservation orchestrator coordinates a reservation from start to finish.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: It asks the stock ledger to reserve the requested quantity, asks the pricing rules for the order's price, and, once both succeed, publishes a StockReserved event to the message broker.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: If the ledger cannot reserve the full quantity, the orchestrator rejects the whole order; it never makes a partial reservation.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: A reservation that is not confirmed within 15 minutes is released by the ledger and the stock becomes available again.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration

units.text: The stock ledger in `src/ledger/ledger.ts` owns stock levels.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: It records every change as an append-only ledger entry (reserve, release, restock) and writes those entries to Postgres.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: The ledger is the only module allowed to write to the stock tables; other modules ask it to make changes.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: The pricing rules in `src/pricing/rules.ts` work out the price of an order from the supplier price lists and any active discounts.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: They read price lists from Redis, where they are cached for 300 seconds, and they never change stock.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: Neither domain module imports anything from `src/api/` or `src/orders/`.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: Dependencies point inwards: the API layer calls the orchestrator, the orchestrator calls the domain modules, and the domain modules depend only on persistence and the platform helpers.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services

units.text: The supplier feed adapter in `src/suppliers/feedAdapter.ts` brings in restocks from suppliers.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration

units.text: Every 10 minutes it calls the supplier API for new deliveries, converts each delivery into a restock and asks the stock ledger to record it.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration

units.text: The adapter is the only module that knows the supplier's data format, so a change on the supplier's side stays inside this one file.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration

units.text: A delivery the adapter cannot parse is logged and skipped; it is not retried, because sending the same bad data again would fail the same way.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration

units.text: Postgres holds the ledger entries and the current stock level per warehouse and product; it is the source of truth for stock.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems

units.text: Redis holds cached price lists and nothing that cannot be rebuilt from the supplier feed.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems

units.text: The message broker carries StockReserved events to other services, such as fulfilment, and also hosts the dead-letter queue described below.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems

units.text: Postgres schema changes live in `db/migrations/` and run on every deploy.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems

units.text: The supplier API is run by the suppliers, outside our control, and is the only external system Shelfwise calls.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems

units.text: Every module logs through the structured logger in `src/platform/log.ts`, which writes one JSON line per event and always includes the correlation ID that the HTTP handlers attached.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: The handlers log each request, and the retry helper logs each failed attempt.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: Calls to the supplier API can fail, so the feed adapter wraps them in the retry helper in `src/platform/retry.ts`.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: The retry policy is:
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: at most 5 attempts per delivery;
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: exponential backoff that starts at 2 seconds, doubles after each failure and is capped at 60 seconds;
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: after the 5th failed attempt, the delivery is published to the dead-letter queue `inventory.dlq` on the message broker, and staff review it in the admin UI.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: Retries apply only to supplier calls.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: Reservations are never retried automatically: a failed reservation is returned to the caller as an error.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling

units.text: New contributors usually start with `src/orders/reserve.ts`, because it shows a whole reservation in about 120 lines and names every module it depends on.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Where to start reading

units.text: After that, `src/ledger/ledger.ts` explains how stock is counted.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Where to start reading

units.text: Each module keeps its tests next to its code.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Where to start reading

units.text: Three rules keep the structure readable.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules

units.text: First, nothing in the domain modules may depend on the HTTP layer; the ledger and the pricing rules must stay usable from a script or a test without a web server.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules

units.text: Second, only the ledger writes stock to Postgres; the orchestrator and the adapter go through it.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules

units.text: Third, only the supplier feed adapter calls the supplier API.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules

units.text: The admin UI has no automated tests yet.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps

units.text: The reservation orchestrator and the feed adapter can both change the same product's stock at once, and the ledger currently relies on a database row lock to keep them consistent; whether that holds under peak load has not been measured.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps

units.text: Dead-lettered deliveries are only found when someone opens the admin UI; nothing alerts the team when `inventory.dlq` starts to fill up.
units.topic: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps
